definitions.explanation: A state of physical or mental comfort and freedom from pain or hardship. Often used in formal or literary contexts.

examples.japanese: {安楽|あんらく}な{生活|せいかつ}を{送|おく}る。
{老後|ろうご}は{安楽|あんらく}に{暮|く}らしたい。
examples.english: I want to live comfortably in my old age.

examples.japanese: {長年|ながねん}{働|はたら}いてきた{祖父|そふ}は、{今|いま}は{田舎|いなか}で{安楽|あんらく}な{毎日|まいにち}を{過|す}ごしている。
examples.english: My grandfather, who worked for many years, now spends peaceful days in the countryside.

notes: Most commonly encountered in the compound {安楽死|あんらくし} (euthanasia, literally 'peaceful death'). Other compounds: {安楽椅子|あんらくいす} (easy chair, armchair). As a standalone adjective, {安楽|あんらく}な has a somewhat formal or literary tone; in everyday speech, {楽|らく} or {快適|かいてき} are more common for describing comfort. Related: {楽|らく} (easy, comfortable — more casual), {快適|かいてき} (comfortable — modern, everyday).
